# Selling the old hatchback

Sold the Astra (WR61 TZB) on 9 August 2025. Six years, 50,000 miles from me, one fractured spring, zero breakdowns on the road (the flat battery doesn't count, it was on the street). Sad for about a minute.

## Valuation

Checked three places, 25 July 2025, 121,800 miles:
- WeBuyAnyCar online: £820, which dropped to £640 "after inspection" according to a mate who tried it with his Corsa
- Motorway: £1,050 highest bid
- Parkers private price, fair condition: £1,500 to £1,800
- Similar Astra J 1.6 with 115k to 125k on Facebook Marketplace in BS postcodes: £1,400 to £2,200

Decided private sale, list at £1,895, accept anything over £1,600.

## Getting it ready

- Full valet myself: snow foam, two-bucket wash, clay bar, Autoglym polish. Inside: vacuum, wet vac on the seats (coffee stain from 2022), Armor All on the plastics. Took a whole Saturday
- Touched up the stone chips on the bonnet, £12 paint pen in Sovereign Silver (Z176)
- New wiper blades, £24, because buyers notice smears
- Fixed the sticky driver's window switch with contact cleaner
- Got every bit of paper in one folder: V5C, both keys, service history, the MOT certificates and the notes from [[MOT failure notes]], receipts for springs, brakes, battery, tyres

## The listing

Facebook Marketplace and Gumtree, 26 July 2025. 22 photos in good daylight, including the tread on all four tyres and the dashboard with no lights on (screenshot of the Foxwell scan with no codes, see [[Dashboard warning lights]]).

Wrote it straight: 121k, known advisory for subframe surface rust, rocker cover gasket done Mar 2025, MOT till March 2026. Included the set of winter tyres on steel wheels (see [[Winter tyres]]) as a sweetener.

## Messages

Got 47 messages in 4 days. Roughly:
- 30 "is this still available?" and nothing after
- 6 lowballs (£700, "cash today")
- 3 obvious scams: a courier will collect, they'll send a cheque, can I pay a "PayPal fee". Blocked
- 1 bloke wanting to swap for a quad bike with no paperwork. No
- 7 genuine questions about timing chain (it's a chain, not a belt, done at 98k by the previous owner, receipt in the folder)

## Viewings

1. 1 Aug, Tom from Kingswood: test drove, liked it, offered £1,400. No
2. 3 Aug, a couple from Bath, didn't turn up
3. 9 Aug, **Gary Pocock** from Weston-super-Mare, buying it for his son who'd just passed his test

Gary brought his own OBD reader, looked under it with a torch, checked the oil and coolant, read the whole folder. Offered £1,600, settled at **£1,650** with the winter tyres.

## Payment and paperwork

- Faster Payments bank transfer while he stood in the kitchen. Waited until it showed as cleared in my banking app, not just "sent". Ref "ASTRA WR61"
- Wrote a receipt in duplicate: date, reg, VIN last 6 (DV2147), mileage 121,930, price, "sold as seen, as tested", both signed
- Told DVLA online the same evening with the 11-digit reference from the V5C. Got the email confirmation, ref DVLA-SN-72016493. Car tax refund for the remaining months arrived 19 days later, £81.25
- Gave Gary the green new keeper slip (V5C/2)
- Cancelled the insurance from 10 Aug, got a pro-rata refund, see [[Car insurance renewal]]
- Removed the car from the Green Flag cover and the ULEZ/CAZ account

## Afterwards

Money went straight into the deposit for the MG, see [[Car loan]]. Gary texted a week later to say his son had done 300 miles in it and loved it. Good.
